content: Diagnosing post-bariatric surgery hypoglycemia (PBSH) requires a thorough evaluation of the patient’s medical history, dietary habits, and activity patterns. It is also essential to rule out other potential causes of hypoglycemia, such as malnutrition, adverse effects of medications, dumping syndrome, or insulinoma. The initial approach to treatment emphasizes dietary modifications. Patients are advised to consume slower-absorbing carbohydrates, adequate protein, and healthy fats to prevent rapid drops in blood glucose levels. Nutritional therapy provided by dietitians with expertise in managing PBSH is strongly recommended. Additionally, the use of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) can be particularly beneficial, especially for individuals who experience hypoglycemia unawareness. If dietary adjustments alone are insufficient, pharmacological interventions may be considered. Medications such as acarbose can be used to slow carbohydrate absorption. Alternatively, agents like diazoxide and octreotide may be employed to reduce the secretion of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and insulin.
